title: Singular and Plural Forms, Spelling, and Pronunciation

sections.learningObjectives:
- Apply rules for forming plurals of medical terms.
- Identify common spelling pitfalls in medical terminology.
- Recognize the importance of accurate spelling and pronunciation in documentation and communication.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of it like turning one leaf into a handful of leaves. The ending changes in a special way instead of just adding an 's'.

### Question 2

One shoulder blade is a scapula; two shoulder blades are scapulae. It is like 'one formula, two formulae'.

### Question 3

It is a pattern, like knowing that 'one cactus' becomes 'many cacti'. Here the pattern is 'one -a, many -ae'.

### Question 4

If you have two cookies, you say 'two cookies,' not 'two cookie.' Medical words follow their own special plural rules.

### Question 5

One kneecap is a patella; a pair of kneecaps are patellae. Same pattern as one formula, two formulae.

### Question 6

One air tube is a bronchus; the two air tubes are the bronchi. The -us ending swaps to -i.

### Question 7

One blood clot is a thrombus; several are thrombi. It follows the same swap as cactus to cacti.

### Question 8

One center is a nucleus; many centers are nuclei. Like one focus, two foci.

### Question 9

One traveling clot is an embolus; more than one are emboli. Same -us to -i swap.

### Question 10

One stone is a calculus; a pile of stones are calculi. Same pattern as cactus to cacti.

### Question 11

If 'alveoli' are many tiny air sacs, one single air sac is an alveolus. Working backward from plural to singular.

### Question 12

Most -us words become -i, but 'virus' is an exception that just takes 'es,' like 'bus' becoming 'buses.'

### Question 13

One tiny germ is a bacterium; a whole crowd of them are bacteria. The -um ending turns into -a.

### Question 14

One pouch is a diverticulum; several pouches are diverticula. The -um swaps to -a.

### Question 15

One egg cell is an ovum; many are ova. The -um ending becomes -a.

### Question 16

One upper heart chamber is an atrium; the two together are the atria. The -um becomes -a.

### Question 17

One dividing wall is a septum; the walls that divide are septa. The -um swaps to -a.

### Question 18

One diagnosis becomes two diagnoses. The -is ending changes to -es.

### Question 19

One site of spread is a metastasis; several are metastases. The -is becomes -es.

### Question 20

One is a testis; the pair are the testes. The -is swaps to -es.

### Question 21

One prediction is a prognosis; several are prognoses. The -is becomes -es.

### Question 22

One look at the data is an analysis; several are analyses. The -is changes to -es.

### Question 23

One appendix becomes two appendices. The -ix ending turns into -ices.

### Question 24

One index, two indices. The -ex ending becomes -ices.

### Question 25

One cervix, two cervices. The -ix ending turns into -ices.

### Question 26

One nerve cluster is a ganglion; several are ganglia. The -on ending becomes -a.

### Question 27

One rule is a criterion; a list of rules are criteria. The -on swaps to -a.

### Question 28

One finger bone is a phalanx; the bones of your fingers are phalanges. The -nx becomes -nges.

### Question 29

One voice box is a larynx; the -nx ending becomes -nges, giving larynges.

### Question 30

One opening is a foramen; several openings are foramina. The -en ending becomes -ina.

### Question 31

One hollow center is a lumen; several are lumina. The -en ending becomes -ina.

### Question 32

One tumor is a carcinoma; the special Latin plural is carcinomata, like stigma becoming stigmata.

### Question 33

One tissue sample is a biopsy; two are biopsies. Just like one baby, two babies.

### Question 34

One chest is a thorax; the -ax ending turns into -aces, giving thoraces.

### Question 35

It is like saying 'several mice' instead of 'several mouse.' The plural has to match the word 'multiple.'

### Question 36

One air tube is a bronchus; the other three choices are all 'more than one' words.

### Question 37

It is like telling 'one dog' from 'many dogs.' 'Vertebrae' is the 'many' form.

### Question 38

It is like matching one sock to its pair. Only 'ganglion and ganglia' is the true matching set.

### Question 39

Think of a key that fits only one lock. For -um words, the key that fits is changing it to -a.

### Question 40

If a note says one broken bone but the patient has three, the doctor might make a mistake. Getting one versus many right protects the patient.

### Question 41

It is like the words 'bear' and 'bare' - they sound alike but mean totally different things. 'Ileum' is gut; 'ilium' is hip bone.

### Question 42

One is a thing (the gooey mucus), and the other is a describing word (a mucous membrane). Like 'glass' versus 'glassy.'

### Question 43

If you have your appendix removed, that is an append-ectomy - the ending means 'take it out.'

### Question 44

When the doctor feels your tummy, that is palpation. When your heart feels fluttery, that is palpitation. One letter changes everything.

### Question 45

When a body part gets red and swollen, we add '-itis' to its name, like 'tonsill-itis' for angry tonsils.

### Question 46

Intra-mural sports are inside one school; inter-mural sports are between schools. 'Intra' is inside, 'inter' is between.

### Question 47

Ab-duct means to carry away; ad-duct means to carry toward. One little letter flips the direction.

### Question 48

Hyper is like a hyper puppy - too much energy. Hypo is the opposite - too little.

### Question 49

'Dys-' is like when something is 'dis-ordered' and not working right - it means hard or painful.

### Question 50

Blood words often end in '-emia.' It is a hint that the condition has to do with blood.

### Question 51

A hemorrhage is when blood bursts out. The '-rrhage' ending means a sudden burst.

### Question 52

Athero- and arterio- sound almost the same, but one means fatty gunk and the other means the blood vessel itself.

### Question 53

A hemisphere is half a sphere. 'Hemi-' means half. Blood is 'hemo-,' not 'hemi-.'

### Question 54

It is spelled hem-or-rhage - notice the double 'r' in the middle. Just remember 'hemo' plus 'rrhage.'

### Question 55

The word has two p's and one c: ap-pen-di-ci-tis. It is like a secret code for 'appendix inflammation.'

### Question 56

Say the word 'school' - the 'ch' sounds like 'k.' Medical 'ch' words like 'chronic' work the same way.

### Question 57

The 'p' is shy and hides. You say 'so-RYE-a-sis,' not 'pso-RYE-a-sis.'

### Question 58

The 'p' is silent, just like in the word 'pneumatic.' You say 'new-MO-nya.'

### Question 59

'Ph' is a two-letter team that makes the 'f' sound, like in 'phone' and 'photo.'

### Question 60

The 'h' is a silent helper. You say 'rye-NYE-tis,' not 'r-hi-NYE-tis.'

### Question 61

Say 'bron-keye' and 'new-clee-eye.' The little 'i' at the end says its own name: 'eye.'

### Question 62

Say 'ver-tuh-bree.' The 'ae' at the end sounds like the letter 'e.'

### Question 63

The 'x' here sounds like a 'z,' just like the start of the name 'Xavier.'

### Question 64

Say 'cat' (hard c) and 'city' (soft c). The vowels e, i, and y make the c turn soft and hiss like an 's.'

### Question 65

The 'g' is silent, like in the word 'gnat.' You say 'nog' + 'NO-sis.'

### Question 66

It is like mixing up 'up' and 'down' on an elevator button. Going the wrong way can be dangerous.

### Question 67

If you cannot read a friend's note, you ask them what it says instead of guessing. The same rule keeps patients safe.

### Question 68

If a coach says 'left' but you thought 'right,' you ask again. Checking the word protects against a big mistake.

### Question 69

It is like searching the internet with the wrong spelling - you might not find what you are looking for.

### Question 70

A record is like a careful diary of what happened. If the words are wrong, the story of the patient's care is wrong.

### Question 71

Palpitation is the fluttery feeling of your heart; palpation is when someone feels your body with their hands.

### Question 72

When you are not sure how to spell a word in a school essay, you look it up. Medical notes deserve the same care.

### Question 73

If everyone uses the same word for the same thing, no one gets confused - like all players knowing the same play calls.

### Question 74

If a short code could mean two things, write the whole word so no one has to guess.

### Question 75

If a friend asks how to say a new word, you say it slowly and maybe write it down. The same kindness helps patients.
